summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with hypotension and chest pain following a dialysis session. Initial concerns included sepsis due to his dialysis line, but blood cultures showed no growth, and antibiotics were discontinued after 48 hours. The hypotension was attributed to fluid removal during dialysis, worsened by diarrhea and poor oral intake. His chest pain resolved in the ED, and serial troponins showed only a minor elevation, consistent with baseline. Diarrhea resolved, and stool studies were negative for pathogens. He remained stable on the medical floor, completed scheduled dialysis, and was discharged home after three days with instructions to follow up with nephrology and cardiology, monitor weight, and start Nephrocaps.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
